application: NFC sticker / URL tag / text tag
summary: Common NFC sticker/tag family often used for URLs, text records and simple automation.

memoryLayout.ndef: NDEF data can contain URL, text, Wi-Fi, vCard and app launch records.

safeRecommendedActions: Check if tag is locked before writing
beginnerExplanation: NFC stickers usually contain human-friendly data such as links or text, not sector/key structures.

cardProfile.name: NTAG21x / NFC Type 2
cardProfile.description: NTAG21x tags are NFC Type 2 tags commonly used for links, text records and product labels. Human-readable content is normally stored as NDEF records when present.
normallyAbsentData: card number in LF access format
limitations: A blank tag may have no NDEF records
Locked or password-protected pages may not be readable
NDEF content depends on what was written by the owner
recommendedNextSteps: Record whether the tag is blank, locked or writable
Save public tag content to inventory
cardProfile.meaning: If an NTAG contains an NDEF record, Electron can show human-friendly data such as a URL or text. If no NDEF record exists, the tag may simply be blank or used by a custom application.
notVisibleReasons: NTAG cards do not normally contain LF facility codes.
A name or expiry date only appears if someone wrote that information as NDEF or custom data.
Password-protected pages are not readable without authorization.

faqs.question: Why does Electron say no NDEF records?
faqs.answer: The tag may be blank, formatted for another application, locked, or using pages that Electron has not read yet.

faqs.question: Is NTAG the same as MIFARE Classic?
faqs.answer: No. NTAG uses page-based NFC Type 2 memory, while MIFARE Classic uses sectors and keys.
